title: refactor: Remove operator!= overloads that C++20 synthesizes
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Removes 40 `operator!=` overloads across 37 files that do nothing but negate the neighbouring `operator==`. Since C++20 the compiler synthesizes these. Also collapses `SHAMapNodeID`'s four relational operators into one `operator<=>`, resolving a `FIXME-C++20` there.

Net effect is 355 lines deleted for 10 added, with no behavior change.

### Context of Change

Since C++20, when the compiler sees `a != b` and finds no viable `operator!=`, it rewrites the expression as `!(a == b)`. It will also consider reversed operands, so a single `operator==` covers `a != b`, `b != a`, `a == b` and `b == a`. That makes a hand-written `operator!=` whose entire body is `return !(lhs == rhs);` dead weight — it has to be kept in sync with `operator==` by hand, and it is one more thing to write for every new comparable type.

**Every removal in this PR is verified by the compiler.** If the rewrite were not viable for some type — an inaccessible `operator==`, a mismatched signature, an ambiguity introduced by the reversed candidate — the call sites would fail to compile rather than silently change meaning. That is the main reason I'd argue this is low-risk despite the file count.

Most of the removals were literally `return !(lhs == rhs);`. Four were spelled differently but are the same predicate:

| Site | Body | Its `operator==` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `STBase::operator!=` | `getSType() != t.getSType() \|\| !isEquivalent(t)` | `getSType() == t.getSType() && isEquivalent(t)` |
| `STArray::operator!=` | `v_ != s.v_` | `v_ == s.v_` |
| `Serializer::operator!=` | `v.data_ != data_` | `v.data_ == data_` |
| `SharedIntrusive::operator!=(nullptr_t)` | `get() != nullptr` | `get() == nullptr` |

`STBase` is a De Morgan expansion; the other three negate exactly the member comparison their `operator==` affirms.

#### `SHAMapNodeID`

This one is a rewrite rather than a deletion. It carried:

```cpp

```

title: test: Use std::string::starts_with/ends_with instead of Boost
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Replaces 26 uses of `boost::starts_with` / `boost::ends_with` with the `std::string` and `std::string_view` member functions, and drops `<boost/algorithm/string/predicate.hpp>` from three of the four files. All call sites are in test code.

### Context of Change

`boost::starts_with` and `boost::ends_with` predate C++20. Since then both `std::string` and `std::string_view` have provided `starts_with` and `ends_with` as members, with the same semantics.

Every operand at these call sites is already a `std::string` or a `std::string_view` — `TrustedPublisherServer.h` uses `std::string_view const path = req.target()`, and the rest are `std::string` — so the substitution is direct rather than a rewrite:

```cpp
// before
if (boost::starts_with(path, "/validators2"))
// after
if (path.starts_with("/validators2"))
```

`ServerStatus_test.cpp` keeps its `predicate.hpp` include because it still calls `boost::iequals`, which has no standard equivalent. (A case-insensitive comparison helper would be a reasonable follow-up, but it needs a home in `StringUtilities` and a decision about locale handling, so it doesn't belong in a substitution-only change.)

title: refactor: Act on TODOs that are unblocked by C++23
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Resolves six `TODO` / `FIXME` comments that were each waiting on a newer language standard or compiler. All of them are unblocked today, so this acts on them and deletes the comments. No behavior changes.

| Site | What it was waiting for |
| --- | --- |
| `FeeVoteImpl.cpp` | structured bindings capturable in a lambda |
| `Invariants_test.cpp` | same |
| `ProtocolVersion.cpp` | `std::is_sorted` in a `constexpr` context |
| `ErrorCodes.cpp` | `consteval` |
| `TestHelpers.h` | a standard library shipping `<ranges>` |
| `ServerDefinitions.cpp` | `std::string::contains` |

### Context of Change

`CMakeLists.txt` has set `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD` to 23 for a while now, and `cmake/XrplSanity.cmake` already requires clang 16 or GCC 12 at minimum. The comments were written when neither was true, and nothing has swept them up since.

Details, in the order they appear in the diff:

- **`ErrorCodes.cpp`** — `sortErrorInfos` is only ever called at compile time, to initialise `kSortedErrorInfos`. It is now `consteval` rather than `constexpr`, which makes that a guarantee instead of a convention.

title: fix: Deduplicate oracle entries in get_aggregate_price RPC
body:
## Summary

The `get_aggregate_price` RPC handler does not deduplicate oracle entries from the user-supplied `oracles` array. A caller can list the same `{account, oracle_document_id}` pair multiple times (up to 200 total entries), causing duplicate price data to be included in aggregate calculations. This makes the response's `size` field misleading and skews the mean/median/standard deviation.

## Changes

- Added a `std::set<std::pair<AccountID, std::uint32_t>>` to track seen `{account, documentID}` pairs during iteration of the oracles array
- Duplicate entries are silently skipped via `emplace().second` check, preventing the same oracle's price data from being inserted into the `Prices` bimap multiple times
- Added `#include <set>` for `std::set`

## Testing

The fix is minimal and non-breaking - duplicate entries are simply skipped after validation. Existing valid requests with unique oracles are completely unaffected. The deduplication happens after input validation, so malformed entries still return the appropriate error.

Fixes #6583

title: fix: Add null check for account object reads
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Adds a defensive null check when `account_objects` reads ledger objects referenced by an account owner directory.

`ReadView::read` documents that it may return `nullptr` if the key is not present or the type does not match. The previous code dereferenced the returned pointer before checking it, which could crash if the directory contained an unreadable or missing object.

This change skips unreadable directory entries before accessing the SLE.

Fixes #7511

### Context of Change

Owner directories should normally reference valid ledger objects, but corrupted or inconsistent ledger state can leave a dangling directory entry. In that case, `ledger.read(keylet::child(*iter))` can return `nullptr`.

The `account_objects` handler previously used the returned pointer immediately through `sleNode->getType()` and `sleNode->getJson(...)` without checking it first. This change makes the code more defensive and avoids dereferencing a null pointer.
